name: pdf_search_finds_a_wrapped_text
why: REPORT 8CD843, ROUND 19 (28/10/2026), observation. A value of four words in a box of the title block was wrapped by SOLIDWORKS over two lines, and «export_pdf» with «search» put it in «not_found» while the PDF printed it. Measured on that PDF: PdfText gives each printed line as a line of its own, the first ending in a space.
defect_caught: A printed text said «not found» because it runs over two lines; and, the other way round, a search that ignores more than the line break, finding a text that is not printed.
_why_a_note_of_two_lines: The wrap of round 19 came from a box too narrow for the value, on a title block of the workshop that the bench does not write. A note with a line break prints the same thing, two lines one under the other, and the bench can write it. If SOLIDWORKS does not take the line break of «note» as a new line, the twin text below says so: it would be found whole, and the case red.

expect.why: the plate the drawing shows: if this does not add up, the drawing below is of another part
a view attaches to the file of the part
from here on the steps measure the drawing
a drawing with a view, as the drawings the search is used on

one line of the note, found as it is printed. Only it: the whole text, if found here, would mean the note was printed on one line, and the case would not measure the wrap
THE FIX: the two lines read as one text across the line break. Until bridge 0.152.9 this text went to «not_found»
THE RED IN THE SAME RUN: the same two lines with the last character changed. Ignoring the line break must not become finding what is not printed
the answer says what a text on several lines asks of whoever reads it: a value wrapped in its box can run out of it, as the second line did in round 19
